Maya S: Drafting PRD + RFC for a runtime-tiering change + sequence-aware kernel selection. Goal: improve latency for short requests and keep unit-cost predictable for long-context customers. Sharing outline and rollout asks.
Liam Chen: Thanks — can you call out explicit acceptance gates and perf experiments?
Maya S: Yes. Top-level acceptance criteria: p95 latency improvement >=15% for seq<=128 on common models, cost delta for seq>1024 within ±5%, no customer-facing errors increase >0.5% during canary.
Anika Patel: Need a clear compatibility matrix for KV storage backends (RAM/NVMe) — some enterprise customers will insist on NVMe-only.
Maya S: Agreed. Adding compatibility table. Also proposing config schema (example):
```json
{
  "runtime_tiers": [
    {"name":"fast","kernels":["fused-attn","matmul-opt"],"max_seq":256,"kv_storage":"mem"},
    {"name":"balanced","kernels":["quant-kernel-v2"],"max_seq":2048,"kv_storage":"nvme"}
  ],
  "sequence_hint_policy":"client-provided|auto-estimate",
  "fallback":"graceful-degrade-to-balanced"
}
```
Oscar R: For sequence_hint_policy, auto-estimate needs a clear heuristic. Suggest: if first request tokens > 80% of recent median, treat as long. Keep thresholds config-driven.
Ryan G: Also list edge cases: 1) sudden sequence spikes (burst long requests), 2) mixed-batch with short+long sequences, 3) KV eviction thrash when many long contexts touch hot keys.
Maya S: Adding edge cases and mitigations: adaptive batching with per-request priority, burst-queue with short-request preemption, and KV hotness smoothing (leaky bucket).
Eva K: For rollout, propose: canary 1% traffic (internal -> select customers), perf harness with synthetic traces (short-only, long-only, mixed), automated rollback on error-rate + tail-latency regression rules.
Anika Patel: + add a quality gate measured by output correctness on our eval suite (we can't break hallucination rates). Suggest baseline eval on 10k prompts, monitor perplexity/ROUGE-like signals for generative tasks.
Maya S: Good point — include eval suite and a checklist: unit tests, end-to-end harness, chaos test (simulate NVMe I/O spikes), cost regression analysis, and a security review for private deployments.
Liam Chen: What's the canary duration? 24-72h? We should also run the perf harness nightly against the canary nodes.
Maya S: Recommend 48h stable window with nightly perf runs; extend if any alert fires. Canary segmentation: 0.5% internal dev, 0.5% opt-in customers.
Oscar R: One more: acceptance criteria for autoscaler interaction. If autoscaler increases nodes, the tier selection shouldn't thrash. Add hysteresis: require 2 consecutive policy votes before moving traffic.
Maya S: Noted. I'll add hysteresis and a metric: churn-rate per-minute < 0.1%.
Ryan G: For the RFC text, include rollout playbook steps with CLI commands for ops: example `redwood runtime promote --tier balanced --percentage 1`. Also a rollback snippet.
Maya S: Adding CLI examples and monitoring dashboards list: p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost per request, KV hit/miss, kernel-switch count, error-rate, and customer-impact tags.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for runtime-tiering-pr-417 on cluster us-west-2-canary at 2025-05-11T15:12:30Z :rocket:
Eva K: Will coordinate with Solutions eng to notify Nimbus Health about canary opt-in. Also flag known incompatible third-party kernel plugins.
Anika Patel: Question: do we need a migration tool for persisted KV formats if we change storage layout? That would be a blocker for Private customers.
Maya S: Yes — include a migration plan with a migration CLI and dry-run mode. Mark as hard dependency for Private deployment GA.
Liam Chen: SGTM. I'll volunteer to own the perf harness spikes detection and alerts.
Maya S: Thanks. Action items: 1) I'll finish PRD + RFC draft with the compatibility matrix and playbook. 2) Liam owns perf harness metrics. 3) Anika owns NVMe migration design. 4) Oscar owns hysteresis and policy heuristics. 5) Ryan writes rollout CLI docs. 6) Eva coordinates customers. Please review the first draft by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Oscar R: Quick nit: add a small section listing known risks and mitigations (data egress for private KV migrations, kernel correctness for quant kernels, increased GPU memory pressure).
Maya S: Will add risk register. Thanks all.
deploy-bot: canary health checks passing (0 errors, avg p95 delta -12% for seq<=128) — monitoring continues.
Liam Chen: Nice numbers. Post the perf run link when available.
Maya S: Will post results + RFC link in #eng-runtime when draft is up.
Eva K: Sg, will ping Nimbus Health once opt-in is confirmed.
Ryan G: I'll draft the rollback steps now and share in thread.
Maya S: Thanks everyone. End of thread for now — will update with PR link.
